lesson_title: Catchment Management: The Fish Tank That Turned Green
hook_text: Over-feed a fish tank and every fish dies — of suffocation, not poison. Now scale it up to a dam.
clip_script: Suppose you feed your fish too generously every day. The extra food dissolves, and the water becomes rich, over-fed water. Green algae cannot believe their luck: they bloom until the glass turns pea-soup green. The murk blocks the light, the plants below die, the algae boom exhausts itself and dies too, and the dead material rots. Rotting uses up oxygen. The fish rise to the surface, gasping, and one morning the tank is silent. That exact story, scaled up to a dam, is eutrophication — feed, bloom, dark, die, rot, suffocate. South Africa's famous green tank is Hartbeespoort Dam.
visual_style: Time-lapse of a fish tank clouding from clear to pea-green, then a match-cut to aerial footage of a green-scummed dam, six beat-words stamping on screen in rhythm: FEED, BLOOM, DARK, DIE, ROT, SUFFOCATE.
pacing: Slow green build, accelerating beats through the chain, silent still tank at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and master the six-beat chain plus the case study that fixes it.
